data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's claim that the expert will outperform fails for a central class of objectively verifiable tasks: those where individual application of the verification procedure is high-variance or error-prone (e.g., visual detection tasks, prolonged multi-step calculations). A non-expert panel applying even a 'lossy compressed' checklist can achieve higher reliability through aggregation canceling individual noise, while a single expert—no matter how well they internalized the verification logic—is subject to a single-instance variance the panel averages out.
